As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to really sit with what we’ve uncovered. The past doesn’t just sit quietly behind us—it shapes the world we live in today. And when we remember, when we choose not to turn away, that’s a powerful act of resistance in itself.
Think about this: every small act of courage can ripple outward. Even the tiniest stand for what’s right can end up changing the course of history. Justice isn’t just about big, sweeping gestures—it’s about being honest, telling the truth, and having the courage to face uncomfortable realities.
Sure, the legacy of exploitation still lingers. But so does the hope for healing. And bearing witness—that isn’t just for a select few. It’s something all of us can do.
If you’ve followed the story of King Leopold’s Congo all the way here, you’ve already taken an important step. You’ve chosen not to look away. This isn’t just a tragedy left behind in history books—it’s a living challenge for all of us. A call to remember, to question, to act.
What happened in the Congo Free State was the result of choices—human decisions that shaped lives and futures. And here’s the thing: our choices today matter just as much.
You don’t have to be a historian or a campaigner to make a difference. It can start with listening to voices that’ve been silenced, asking questions about the world around you, and noticing the ways history still echoes in our present. Support those working for justice—whether they’re close to home or on the other side of the world.
Most of all, remember this: being a witness—seeing, remembering, and speaking the truth—that’s a way to push back against despair. It’s a real act of hope.
The ghosts of the past aren’t here to haunt us. They’re here to remind us of our shared humanity. By honoring their memory, we tap into our own ability for empathy, courage, and change.
The work isn’t finished. But every step forward—no matter how small—is worth taking. And every new generation gets a chance to begin again.
